items.title: 6.2.7 Length of the Tangent from a Point to a Circle (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 180-181: 6.2.7 Theorem 3 (length of tangent) with Proof and Figure 6.9

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein hum ne bahar ke point se tangents ki equations nikalin. Ab ek aur aam sawal: point se point of contact tak tangent ka tukra (segment) kitna lamba hai? Is ka ek bohat saada formula hai, aur us ke peeche sirf Pythagoras theorem hai jo aap barson se jaante hain. Yeh lambai exam mein seedhe sawal ke taur par bhi aati hai, aur aage do circles ke sawalon mein bhi kaam aati hai. Aaiye dekhte hain.

Theorem 3: The length of the tangent drawn from a point \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) to the circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) is
\[\sqrt{x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Ghor kijiye: square root ke andar jo expression hai woh bilkul wahi hai jo 6.2.4 ke Theorem 1 mein tha, yani circle ki equation ke left side mein point rakhne se jo value aati hai. Wahan us ka sign dekha tha, yahan us ka square root le rahe hain.

Saboot (Proof): circle ka centre \(C(-g, -f)\) aur radius \(r = \sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\) maan lijiye. \(PT\) point \(P\) se circle par tangent hai jo circle ko \(T\) par chhoota hai. To \(CT \perp PT\).
Right triangle \(PTC\) mein (Pythagoras theorem se):
\[|PT|^{2} = |PC|^{2} - |CT|^{2}\]
Jahan,
\[|PC|^{2} = (x_{1} + g)^{2} + (y_{1} + f)^{2}\]
\[|CT|^{2} = r^{2} = g^{2} + f^{2} - c\]
Is liye,
\[|PT|^{2} = (x_{1} + g)^{2} + (y_{1} + f)^{2}\]
\[- (g^{2} + f^{2} - c)\]
\[= x_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + g^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2fy_{1}\]
\[+ f^{2} - g^{2} - f^{2} + c\]
\[= x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c\]
Lehaza,
\[|PT| = \sqrt{x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c}\]

blocks.alt: A circle with centre C(-g, -f). From an outside point P(x1, y1) on the right, two tangents touch the circle; the upper point of contact is T. The radius CT is drawn and the right angle at T between CT and the tangent PT is marked 90 degrees. The segment CP joins the centre to P.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.9: Tangent PT from P(x1, y1) to the circle with centre C(-g, -f); CT is perpendicular to PT (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Poora saboot sirf Pythagoras hai. Point of contact par radius tangent ke perpendicular hota hai, is liye \(C\), \(T\), \(P\) ek right triangle banate hain jis ka right angle \(T\) par hai aur hypotenuse (sab se lambi side) \(CP\) hai. Is liye \(|PT|^{2} = |PC|^{2} - |CT|^{2}\).
Expand karne ke baad \(g^{2}\) aur \(f^{2}\) cancel ho jate hain; is liye centre ya radius alag se nikalne ki zaroorat nahin parti, seedha point ko equation mein rakh dein.
Square root ke andar wala number \(S_{1} = |CP|^{2} - r^{2}\) hai. Is liye:
\(S_{1} > 0\) (bahar): real tangent, lambai \(\sqrt{S_{1}}\);
\(S_{1} = 0\) (circle par): lambai 0, point khud apna point of contact hai;
\(S_{1} < 0\) (andar): koi real tangent nahin, jo Theorem 2 se milta hai.
Ek point se dono tangents barabar lambe hote hain: dono right triangles ki hypotenuse \(CP\) ek hi hai aur dono ka radius barabar hai. Jaise kisi khambe se do barabar rassiyan zameen par gol daire ke do kinaron tak bandhi hon.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal kitab ki nahin. Point \(P(4, -1)\) se circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x + 4y = 0\) (Example 14 wala circle) par tangent ki lambai:
\[|PT| = \sqrt{16 + 1 - 8 - 4} = \sqrt{5}\]
Example 14 se tasdeeq: point of contact \((3, -3)\) ka \(P\) se faasla \(\sqrt{(4 - 3)^{2} + (-1 + 3)^{2}} = \sqrt{1 + 4} = \sqrt{5}\) hai, aur \((2, 0)\) ka bhi \(\sqrt{4 + 1} = \sqrt{5}\). Dono barabar, aur formula ke jawab ke barabar!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Origin \((0, 0)\) se circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x - 8y + 9 = 0\) par tangent ki lambai kya hogi? (Jawab: \(\sqrt{0 + 0 - 0 - 0 + 9} = 3\). Jab point origin ho to lambai sirf \(\sqrt{c}\) hai.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) se tangent ki lambai: \(\sqrt{x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c}\).
2. Yeh right triangle \(PTC\) mein Pythagoras se aati hai: \(|PT|^{2} = |PC|^{2} - r^{2}\).
3. Ek point se dono tangents barabar lambe hote hain.
4. \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients 1 hone chahiye (6.2.8 dekhiye).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(r^{2}\) ko minus ki jagah plus kar dena: \(|PT|^{2} = |PC|^{2} - r^{2}\), kyun ke hypotenuse \(CP\) hai.
2. \(5x^{2} + 5y^{2} + \ldots = 0\) jaisi equation ko pehle 5 se taqseem kiye baghair formula laga dena; jawab \(\sqrt{5}\) guna bara aa jayega.
3. Root ke andar negative number aaye aur yeh na samajhna ke point circle ke andar hai.
